clue.text: Coat as a remedy for 7?

definitions.meaning: a dog's coat is literally its fur
the proverbial cure for a hangover after a night out is another drink

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a hound's fur and the morning drink taken to ease a hangover after a wild night.

clue.text: Abrasive words maybe heard in 7

parts.note: a drinking toast heard in the pub on a wild night, whose words literally describe an abrasion to the face

explanation.walkthrough: 'Abrasive' looks like rude, but it means scraping skin: the toast literally describes a graze.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a jocular British drinking toast, said when raising a glass, which literally pictures a scraped face.

clue.text: Bagels — same order for a party

indicators.note: putting things in order rearranges them, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Bagels are ordered in the same batch for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: An assemblage is a gathering of people, which is one sense of party.

clue.text: Letter demands no duck shooter in quarters

indicators.note: the gun is placed inside the two compass points

parts.note: E (east) is a compass quarter; two quarters give two Es

indicators.note: no means the duck is left out of the gun

parts.note: a shooter is a gun such as a pistol
a duck in cricket is a score of nought, the letter O

explanation.surface: A letter requests that a shooter with no ducks to aim at stay in his quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove O from PISTOL to get PISTL, then put it between two Es. In cricket a duck is a score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a letter, especially a formal or biblical one.

clue.text: Chinese date plum said to be a military shade

indicators.note: said signals that the word is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: khaki is the dull brownish colour of army uniforms

explanation.surface: A fruit is described as being the colour of army uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: The kaki is the Japanese persimmon, also known as the Chinese date plum.

clue.text: Offer of euthanasia in 7?

parts.note: a barman's question on a night out, read literally as offering someone a lethal dose

explanation.definitionFit: This is the jocular question used to ask which drink someone would like, read literally as offering a deadly dose.

clue.text: Not the hit single played again for mad celebration

indicators.note: playing a song again in a new version reworks the letters

explanation.surface: A DJ plays a track that was never a hit single at a wild party.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild evening out of partying and drinking is an idiom for a mad celebration.

clue.text: Moggy about to grab fish causes commotion

indicators.note: grabbing puts the fish within the reversed cat
about means the word for cat is turned round

parts.note: moggy is a British informal word for a cat, a puss
hake is a sea fish

explanation.surface: A cat about to seize a fish throws the household into uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns PUSS into SSUP; HAKE goes inside after the first S.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir things up or cause a commotion is a common phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Banish rubbish here

indicators.note: rubbish as a verb says the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to get rid of rubbish in a particular place.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes a receptacle where you throw away rubbish such as ashes.

clue.text: Progress may be pending in church

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a matter pending is left hanging, so pending suggests hang

explanation.surface: Advances may be awaiting approval from the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Progress is a form of development or alteration, a near synonym in the sense of moving on.

clue.text: Trees — that's his fixation

indicators.note: to fix something can mean to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Shittah trees are acacias mentioned in the Bible, the plural naming several such trees.

clue.text: In London one's called dishonest for property holding

indicators.note: in a Cockney London accent the th sound is spoken as f

parts.note: a dishonest person is a thief

explanation.surface: In London someone is branded a cheat over a property holding.
explanation.definitionFit: A fief was land held by a vassal from a feudal lord, an estate or property holding.

clue.text: Byron's composition brought to account by writer

indicators.note: the anagram is brought next to the account, following it

parts.note: a bill is an account of money owed

indicators.note: composing arranges material, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the poet's name with its s gives the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A poem by Byron is charged to an author's account.
explanation.definitionFit: The American-born travel writer is known for humorous books about Britain.

clue.text: Official procedure possibly concluding 7

parts.note: a police roadside check for alcohol that may end a night of drinking

explanation.definitionFit: A police check of alcohol levels in a driver is an official procedure that can end a night out.

clue.text: Plant of a type featured in Monopoly game

indicators.note: featured in says the letters sit within the following words

explanation.surface: A kind of plant appears in a board game.
explanation.definitionFit: A polygam is a botanical term for a plant with both bisexual and single-sex flowers.

clue.text: Back pay? The reverse for soldiers, indeed

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
quite as an exclamation of agreement means indeed

explanation.surface: Soldiers indeed are owed back pay.
explanation.walkthrough: Back pay reversed is 'pay back', which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To repay or return something done is to pay it back, the sense of the definition.

clue.text: Tossing caber around the city is novel

indicators.note: the anagram goes around the city letters
tossing throws the letters into a new order

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: Throwing the caber around the city is a new idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tossing' turns CABER into REBCA; EC goes inside after REB. Tossing the caber is a Scottish Highland Games event.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne du Maurier's famous novel bears this title.

clue.text: Harmonisation needs much attention without having people turn back

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the shortened word surrounds
much of the word only, so its last letters are dropped
back means people and turn are read backwards together

parts.note: men are people
a U-turn, so turn gives U

explanation.surface: Getting in harmony requires much attention without people turning back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'much' drops ION from ATTENTION to give ATTENT; 'back' turns MEN + U into UNEM, which goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Attunement is the bringing of things into harmony, so harmonisation.

clue.text: A thick-skinned PM?

parts.note: a British prime minister of the 1840s whose name is also the skin of fruit

explanation.definitionFit: Sir Robert of that name was a Victorian prime minister, and the word also means a fruit's outer rind.

clue.text: Typical model openable with training

indicators.note: training shapes something into a new form, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A fashion model can be opened up with some training.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanpole is a tall, very thin person, as fashion models often are.

clue.text: They take sides in a row

definitions.text: They take sides in a row

parts.words: They take sides in a row
parts.note: rowing blades sit on each side of a boat as it is rowed, not partisans in a quarrel

explanation.definitionFit: Rowing blades are positioned on the boat's sides when people row.

clue.text: Fool catches a smacker, which isn't very bright

indicators.note: catching holds the other letters inside

parts.note: a twit is a fool
a means one, the Roman numeral I
a smacker is slang for a pound, L

explanation.surface: A fool receives a kiss, which isn't very clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilit means lit by twilight, hence dim and not very bright.

clue.text: Tom's second employer

definitions.note: read as Tom is, a tomcat being what is defined

parts.note: mo is short for a moment, a second
a user is someone who employs something

explanation.surface: Tom works for his second boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat that catches mice is a mouser, and a tomcat is one.

clue.text: A patron when disgruntled can be ugly

definitions.meaning: a patron of a shop is someone who buys there
an ugly sort is a difficult, threatening person, especially an angry one

explanation.definitionFit: A patron of a shop is a buyer, and an ugly one is a nasty, difficult character.
